hints.title: Monotonicity Observation
hints.text: If a maximum difference threshold L is achievable with at most k partitions, any larger threshold is also valid.

hints.title: Greedy Interval Partitioning
hints.text: For a candidate threshold L, greedily extend the current segment until the difference between maximum and minimum exceeds L.

hints.title: Subarray Budget Check
hints.text: Verify whether the total number of segments formed does not exceed the allotted budget k.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def minStabilityFactor(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        # A partition into at most k subarrays
        # Stability factor is max(max(sub) - min(sub))
        def check(limit: int) -> bool:
            parts = 1
            curr_min = nums[0]
            curr_max = nums[0]
            for x in nums[1:]:
                n_min = min(curr_min, x)
                n_max = max(curr_max, x)
                if n_max - n_min > limit:
                    parts += 1
                    curr_min = x
                    curr_max = x
                    if parts > k:
                        return False
                else:
                    curr_min = n_min
                    curr_max = n_max
            return parts <= k

        low = 0
        high = max(nums) - min(nums) if nums else 0
        ans = high
        
        while low <= high:
            mid = (low + high) // 2
            if check(mid):
                ans = mid
                high = mid - 1
            else:
                low = mid + 1
                
        return ans
```

variables: max_diff: max element minus min element
complexity.notes: Binary search on difference limit with linear greedy partition verification.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all combinations of partition split points has exponential cost.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct tracking of rolling minimum and maximum uses O(1) space.
